about: THE LENDER'S STICK (8 Oct 2026, night; Design/DECISIONS.md 104 and 105). The debt for the boat in a game begun through the opening (flag lender_opening), owed to Wursing, called the Wōkerer: his man who keeps turning up to ask for something on the stick (DECISIONS 33: the user's own idea; any sum may be paid, wherever he finds her), the day itself and the days after it (unpaid, she works for the lender: half of what she sells goes to the stick until it is clean), and the stick made clean. The count's old chain (chain_house_debt_793.json) sleeps in such a game. Flags: wk_met (he has been met), wk_wait_far / wk_wait_mid / wk_wait_near (lapsing: he does not come while the one for the season stands), wk_hid_grace (falls by four each time she hides: the odds of it being funny fall with it), wk_work (she works for him), wk_clean (the stick is given up). Words: Data/writing/wokerer.json. EVERY WORD IS A PLACEHOLDER for the user's own, and the man's name (Bubo) is the user's to give. FROM 9 OCT 2026 THE LENDER SENDS HIS MEN (Code/Game/Voyage/Collectors.cs, Game/Data/collectors_793.json; the user: 'Sends his goons to collect', 'A handful of times', 'Just clueless brutes'): the man's own three cards (at home, away, alongside in fog) are gone, his words kept in the writing for the user, and two cards stand in their place: the rope men at the quay and alongside at sea (harbour.goons.quay, sea.goons.alongside), never drawn, put first in line when their boat has caught her. FROM 9 OCT 2026, RAVN'S DEATH AND THE FEUD (Code/Game/Voyage/Feud.cs, Game/Data/feud_rules_793.json; the user: 'Ravn needs an impactful death scene as genuine punishment for not repaying the debt but opens up a bloodfued opportunity'): seven cards more (crew.feud.oath, crew.feud.burial, crew.feud.pyre, crew.feud.killer, harbour.feud.door, harbour.feud.court, harbour.feud.outlaw), and the rope men's two cards have a line more for when he is dead. The one who did it has a card of his own, put before theirs, because a card holds nine choices at most and a choice that cannot be taken is still shown.

cards.note: THE LENDER'S MEN HAVE FOUND HER AT A QUAY (the user, 9 Oct 2026: 'Sends his goons to collect'; Code/Game/Voyage/Collectors.cs puts this card first in line when they catch her: it is never drawn). She may pay a pound, two, or all; give cargo at their price; or try a way round them. Each way is carried by one of her stats (goons.ease_X), is harder each time it has fooled them and for each later sending. Given nothing, what they do DEPENDS (law goons_teeth: the lender's temper, what is aboard, whether she has just made fools of them): they talk, or take silver and cargo, or beat a man, or kill one; and the third time she does not pay it is Ravn (they say so the time before). The rope men are clueless brutes, in the user's own words; Bubo is with them to count. EVERY WORD IS A PLACEHOLDER.

cards.note: MICHAELMAS, and every day after it while the stick is not clean and she does not yet work for him (DECISIONS 104, decided by me, the user's to overrule). The lender asks for all of it. Paid: the stick is clean (then: the clean stick). Not paid: he may ask back no more than the sum (the law of 789), so he takes the boat's work: from now half of what she sells goes to the stick before it reaches the purse (flag wk_work, Trade.WorkShare), until it is clean. Nothing is added to the debt, and the game does not end.

She may call the one who did it out of the yard (when no boat of them is out), or go in to the lender himself: he dead, nothing is owed, his men come no more, and she is an outlaw in the Franks' ports until his price is paid. cards.note: THE ONE WHO DID IT (Feud.cs puts this card first in line, ahead of the rope men's own, each time they have caught her while the matter is open and he lives: never drawn). Kill him, or not now. A fight is carried by her nerve, her men against theirs, and weapons aboard (feud.fight). Won: it is answered, and the rest go home. Lost: a man of hers is dead, and they do what they do when they are angry. It is a card of its own because a card holds nine choices at most, and a choice that cannot be taken is still shown: on their own card it would have stood there, greyed, with Ravn alive.
